q: You want to implement an upstream PR in goose. Per AGENTS.md, when may you start coding?
options: When the issue is on the board with Status Ready
As soon as you have read the issue title
When the issue is in Inbox, to help speed triage
Only after a maintainer assigns it to you in a comment
explanation: Reading the title gives you the topic, not the agreed scope and verification plan.
Inbox issues are explicitly NOT to be implemented; help resolve the discussion instead.
Assignment is not the gate — board Status Ready is.

q: Why does the repo set `blank_issues_enabled: false` in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml?
options: So every issue must come through a structured template the maintainers can triage
So only organization members can create issues
So issues are closed automatically after 30 days of inactivity
So issue titles cannot contain special characters
explanation: It does not restrict who can file — it restricts the form of the filing.
Staleness automation lives in .github/workflows/stale.yml, not the template config.
Title character policy is not part of the template configuration.

q: The feature_request template asks "What problem would this solve?" BEFORE implementation details. What is the triage reason behind this order?
options: It forces outcome-first thinking so maintainers can judge the idea without debating a specific implementation
It saves storage space in the issue database
GitHub renders only the first section of a template
Implementation details are forbidden in goose issues entirely
explanation: Storage is not a reason for template section ordering.
All template sections render; ordering is about reading flow, not rendering.
Approaches are explicitly welcome — but after the problem and outcome, not before.

q: Which of these is a real rule from AGENTS.md about `gh issue create`?
options: It does not apply templates automatically; structure the issue on the matching template yourself
It refuses to post unless the issue links a pending PR
It auto-assigns the issue to a random maintainer
It requires a diagnostics zip attachment before running
explanation: gh has no requirement to link a PR at creation time.
gh does not auto-assign issues; assignment is not part of issue creation at all.
Diagnostics zips are requested inside the bug template, not enforced by gh.

q: An issue is marked Needs info. Your best contributor move is:
options: Answer the maintainer's open question to unblock triage
Open a PR implementing your best guess so the discussion is concrete
Close the issue and reopen it with a better title
Ping the maintainer daily until they reply
explanation: A PR before the design is agreed implements a guess and wastes review effort.
Closing/reopening churns the board history and loses context.
Daily pings are noise, not signal — that violates the communication rules.

q: During implementation you find that the agreed design cannot handle a case the issue mentioned. Per AGENTS.md:
options: Return to the issue before continuing, because this is a material design change
Implement both your design and the agreed design behind a config flag
Silently choose the approach that costs fewer lines and mention it in the PR title
File a second duplicate issue and implement from that one
explanation: Doubling the design multiplies review and maintenance burden for a mid-PR shift.
Silent deviation breaks the issue as source of truth — reviewers cannot track it.
A duplicate fragments the discussion; the original issue already owns the context.

q: Fix this process error: a coworker runs `gh issue create` with a one-line body saying they will fill in the template later. The error to flag is:
options: The repo requires template structure at creation time — the issue will land malformed for triage
gh issue create cannot run without a body at all
The issue will be auto-closed by ci.yml
One-line bodies are fine as long as the title has a type prefix
explanation: The command ran; the failure is structural, not that gh refused to run.
No workflow closes issues for short bodies.
A good title does not supply To Reproduce / Expected behavior.
